4.3.1.16.2 Large Data Path in COM
The rules for the decision whether to use Large Data Path in COM are described in System Template [8] Chapter 6.2.1 “Large Data Path in COM”.
[SWS_Rte_01376] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00246
⌈The RTE shall use Large Data Path in COM for sending/receiving arrays of bytes if the ComIPduLargeData is set to TRUE in ComIPdu.⌋ Transmission
[SWS_Rte_01377] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00231
⌈The RTE shall use the Com_Transmit API if ComIPduLargeData is set to TRUE in ComIPdu.⌋ In case If-API is used upon Com_Transmit, the transmit request is passed immediately to the lower layer. After return of the API the data does not need to be locked.
[SWS_Rte_01378] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00231
⌈The RTE shall use the Com_Transmit API if ComIPduType is set to NORMAL in ComIPdu.⌋ In case TP-API is used, after Com_Transmit one or more invocations of the respective Rte_COMCbkCopyTxData notification callback by Large Data Path in COM will occur asynchronously. The Transmission is finalized by the invocation of Rte_COMCbkTpTxConfirmation notification callback as well. During this time the data has to be available for being passed to Large Data Path in Com.
[SWS_Rte_01379] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00246
⌈The RTE shall lock the signal buffer after it initiated a Tp Transmission (Com_Transmit returned E_OK).⌋ During the signal buffer is locked no further transmit requests are permitted on that item. For data semantics this means that Rte_Write/Rte_Call will return RTE_E_COM_BUSY.
[SWS_Rte_01380] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00246
⌈The RTE shall unlock the signal buffer after Rte_COMCbkTpTxConfirmation notification callback has been invoked (independent of the result).⌋
[SWS_Rte_01381] Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00246
⌈The RTE shall copy the indicated number of bytes to the provided destination in each invocation of Rte_COMCbkCopyTxData notification callback.⌋
